meta.purpose: Repository-grounded project context for contributors and AI coding assistants.
meta.usage_instruction: Read this file before making project changes. Distinguish implemented behavior from planned specifications. Values marked proposed or unknown require confirmation before being treated as authoritative. Never add real secrets or credentials to this file.

project.name: PoshanAI
project.tagline: Nutrition awareness and meal-planning for everyday Indian food.
project.problem: People need nutrition information and meal suggestions that are understandable, practical, and relevant to familiar Indian foods.
project.solution: A web application intended to provide nutrition awareness, report-based insights, and personalized meal planning. The existing repository currently contains an Express API foundation and a responsive React frontend; several product features remain planned.
project.core_innovation: Proposed: combine OCR of nutrition reports with Indian food context and personalized meal suggestions. The repository README identifies OCR, IFCT retrieval, and Gemini meal-plan generation as intended capabilities, not completed capabilities.
target_users: People who want meal suggestions based on familiar Indian foods

phase_plan.scope: Monorepo, frontend shell, Express API, MongoDB connection, authentication foundation, and local development setup.
User profile, report upload/storage, OCR processing, and extracted nutrition data.
Indian food context, IFCT retrieval, and personalized meal plans.
Tests, production configuration, observability, and deployment readiness.

backend_env.PORT: Backend port; backend config defaults to 5000. Docker Compose currently maps host/container port 4000 and must be reconciled before using that container setup.
backend_env.JWT_SECRET: Optional shared JWT secret fallback; do not store the real value here.
backend_env.JWT_ACCESS_SECRET: Optional access-token signing secret; falls back to JWT_SECRET.
backend_env.JWT_REFRESH_SECRET: Optional refresh-token signing secret; falls back to JWT_SECRET.
backend_env.CLIENT_URL: Allowed frontend origin; falls back to CLIENT_ORIGIN and then http://localhost:5173.
backend_env.GEMINI_API_KEY: Optional/planned AI integration credential; keep secret and server-side.
backend_env.REDIS_URL: Optional. When configured and available, report OCR is queued; otherwise uploads run OCR synchronously. Default Compose configuration points to its Redis service.

frontend_env.VITE_API_URL: Optional API base URL; frontend Axios client defaults to /api.
frontend_env.VITE_*_SECRET: Never expose secrets through Vite environment variables because they are bundled into browser code.

backend: Use JavaScript ES modules and .js file extensions in imports.
Use two-space indentation, semicolons, and single-quoted strings, matching existing source.
Keep route registration in routes, request orchestration in controllers, persistence shape in models, and reusable business logic in services.
Validate external input with Joi and return the repository's standard success/error JSON envelope.
Use async error forwarding compatible with Express 4.
frontend: Use React function components and JSX.
Keep API calls in src/api and use the shared Axios client.
general: Prefer small, surgical changes and preserve established naming and formatting.
Do not claim placeholder endpoints or AI capabilities are implemented.

security_rules: Never commit .env files, API keys, passwords, access tokens, refresh tokens, or credential-bearing connection strings.
Keep server credentials out of frontend VITE_* variables and browser bundles.
Protect private API routes with the existing JWT access-token middleware.
Determine resource ownership from the authenticated user identity, never a client-supplied owner ID.
Validate request data with Joi; reject unexpected or malformed inputs.
For file uploads, enforce file size and allowed content types; do not trust the client filename or MIME type alone.
Generate server-side random filenames and prevent path traversal; store uploads outside publicly served static roots.
Do not execute, render, or publicly serve uploaded content by default.
Clean up stored files when a database operation fails or when an owned resource is deleted, without deleting files outside the configured upload directory.
Use Helmet, restricted CORS, request-size limits, Mongo operator sanitization, and rate limits already present in the backend.
Do not log secrets, raw authentication tokens, or sensitive health information.
Treat OCR and generative AI output as untrusted input; validate it and do not present it as medical diagnosis.
Return non-revealing production errors; never disclose stack traces, database details, or secret configuration.

git_workflow.branching: Use focused feature branches; examples currently present include feature/frontend-ui and feature/backend-api.
git_workflow.commit_style: Recent repository commits primarily use Conventional Commit prefixes such as feat:, chore:, and perf:.
git_workflow.pull_requests: Use pull requests for review when available.
safety: Do not amend existing commits unless explicitly requested.
Do not force-push unless explicitly requested.
Inspect git status before staging and preserve unrelated working-tree changes.

recommended: Create a local .env from .env.example and configure valid non-production secrets.
Run docker compose up --build from the repository root.
Open the frontend at http://localhost:8080 when using the Compose setup.
direct_local: Ensure MongoDB is running and MONGODB_URI points to it.
Redis and REDIS_URL are optional; without an available Redis service, report uploads process OCR synchronously.
Install dependencies in the root, poshanai-backend, and poshanai-frontend as needed.
Run npm run dev from the repository root to start the API and web development servers.
how_to_start_project.health_check: The backend exposes GET /health. Confirm the actual mapped port using docker-compose.yml and backend configuration; current files have a port configuration mismatch that should be reconciled.

ai_prompt_guidelines: Read this context and the relevant source files before changing code.
Confirm whether schema and behavior are implemented, proposed, or unknown.
Use repository patterns and make focused, testable changes.
Do not invent credentials, secrets, clinical rules, nutrition thresholds, or unprovided schema details.
Validate all model/OCR output before persistence or display.
Keep product language educational and do not claim that PoshanAI diagnoses or replaces qualified healthcare advice.
Report tests run and any pre-existing failures accurately.

do_not: Do not commit or reveal real secrets, API keys, JWT secrets, passwords, or Atlas credentials.
Do not trust req.body.userId or any other client-provided identity to establish ownership.
Do not accept arbitrary file types or unbounded uploads.
Do not use user-controlled filenames as filesystem paths.
Do not expose uploads through an unrestricted static file server.
Do not silently swallow errors or return success-shaped fallback data.
Do not claim planned AI, OCR, IFCT, or meal-planning functionality is operational before verifying it.
Do not provide medical diagnoses or present generated nutrition suggestions as professional medical advice.
Do not force-push, amend commits, or discard unrelated user work without explicit authorization.
